Read only source /evidence/source.json, parent /evidence/parent.json, and independent audit /evidence/audit.json. Do not use the web, any prior-run file other than those exact sealed inputs, any other solution, or any verification report. You may create exact-arithmetic checks only under /work; do not modify files outside /work.

Parent SHA-256: 487f3ac59bbe80c331f0f86b77b25ee7da0acbb9dc4bb9c55a8859bda490d564
Audit SHA-256: 8b33f5cf0458584756f2bd68b27a466cb4fb46005dce8a2896b9ea2d864d5757

This is an exact-closure attempt after the three scheduled search lenses. Concentrate on resolving the independent audit. If no material proof change is required, copy claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch, and final_writeup from the parent exactly.

Address every REFUTED or UNRESOLVED claim and the audit's target-coverage judgment. Preserve correct progress. Repair, narrow, replace, or remove unsupported claims. Never call the open target solved without a complete proof at the requested strength. Put every load-bearing claim in a separate results item in proof order. There is no claim-count cap. The entire ordered proof is in scope. Keep final_writeup under 3,000 words and each proof_sketch under 500 words.

      "idx": 0,
      "claim": "For the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm, every actual queue Q_t is duplicate-free and has exactly the current descent bottoms; processing (p_t,Q_t) yields p_{t+1}=reverse(Q_t) followed by the stable deletion of Q_t from p_t, and the complexity is Θ(n+M_FIFO), where M_FIFO=Σ_t|Q_t|.",
      "claim_sha256": "459468c5e760ab0b611bc6308070a35ef99839d0e842578989c14fd858fa6c5e",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "At a round boundary, deleting all distinct queued values and prepending them in FIFO order directly gives reverse(Q_t) followed by the unqueued values in their old relative order. The front test records exactly the descents introduced within that reversed prefix and at its boundary. Between two surviving unqueued values, the deleted queued run is decreasing in shelf order; as its members are removed, the exposed predecessor increases through that run and crosses the surviving successor's value at most once. The deletion test records exactly that crossing, so no descent bottom is omitted or duplicated. Induction from the initialization scan proves the queue invariant. Initialization costs Θ(n), and every queue occurrence performs Θ(1) linked-list and FIFO work, yielding Θ(n+M_FIFO).",

    },
    {
      "idx": 1,
      "claim": "There is an exact phase decomposition: if i is the largest unfixed value and starts its phase at position s_i, that phase makes exactly (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t moves, where ℓ_t counts its round-t queued elements initially left of i.",

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "All values larger than i occupy a permanent fixed suffix, so i is left of position i and is not queued. In a phase round, removing and prepending a queued element initially left of i has net zero effect on i's position; doing so for an element initially right of i advances i by one. If r_t is the right-side count, the round has ℓ_t+r_t moves and advances i by r_t. Before fixation, i's right neighbor is smaller and therefore queued, so r_t≥1. Summing position advances gives Σ_t r_t=i−s_i, and summing moves gives the claimed identity.",
      "witness": "The checker validated the identity phase by phase on exhaustive traces through n=7, a deterministic sample at n=9, and every A_k trace for k=1 through 80.",
      "search_method": "Exact positional accounting and phase-by-phase trace validation.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/fun2026_optimized_magazine_steps/audit/plain/attempt_4/fun2026_attempt4_exact_checker.py"

      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Within each pair (k+j,j), j is a descent bottom. Every boundary from j to k+j+1 is an ascent, as is k to 3k+1. The boundary 3k+1 to 2k+1 contributes the sole additional descent bottom, and the remaining tail is increasing. The initialization scan therefore produces exactly the asserted FIFO order.",

      "claim_sha256": "5b18621f5e8bf5567e1419ce7730d5b415ac7d005cf011010ff50ca29a028f01",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Claim 2 supplies the base. In the induction step, each displayed j has Prev(j)=j+1 at the round start. Processing 1 creates no event. For j≥2, the preceding processed value j−1 is the front, so the front test appends j−1; the deletion test cannot precede it because it would require an integer strictly between j and j+1. Thus the next queue first receives 1 through k−t−1. The unchanged adjacency a,c_t,c_{t+1} then makes the deletion test for c_t append c_{t+1}, before its front test or any event caused by the undisplayed suffix. This proves the ordered prefix for all required t.",

      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/fun2026_optimized_magazine_steps/audit/plain/attempt_4/fun2026_attempt4_exact_checker.py"

Then R(n)≥⌊(n−1)/3⌋−1 for n≥4, and hence R(n)=Ω(n). Therefore a charging proof that charges every move to its actual predecessor–descent-bottom pair cannot impose a uniform O(1) capacity per pair.",

The displayed lower bound and Ω(n) conclusion follow, and the repeated use of one actual triggering pair directly rules out a uniform constant capacity for that charging rule.",

Since k=n/3+O(1), the bound is Ω(n²); Claim 0 transfers this move lower bound to step complexity.",

The draft proves neither a matching O(n²) upper bound nor a superquadratic lower bound, so it correctly leaves the tight asymptotic target unresolved.",
